passages.title: Urban Green Roofs
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of environment, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: Green roofs can lower surface temperatures in densely built neighbourhoods. Growing layers and vegetation retain some rainfall before it reaches drains.
Deeper growing media can support a wider range of plant species. Designers should plan safe maintenance access before construction begins.
Installation may cost more initially than a conventional roof. Energy savings depend partly on the building's design and use.
Native species may need less watering when suited to local conditions. Engineers must check that a roof can carry the additional weight.

passages.title: The Science of Sleep
passages.intro: An academic-style overview of health science, examining evidence and practical implications.
paras: During sleep, the brain processes and consolidates some newly learned information. Exposure to light influences the timing of the body's internal clock.
Sleep requirements vary between individuals, even within the same age group. A consistent sleep and waking schedule may support sleep quality.
Caffeine can affect alertness for several hours after consumption. Researchers measure both sleep duration and how restorative it is.
Short awakenings occur naturally during many people's nights. Using electronic devices late at night can postpone bedtime.

passages.title: Public Transport and City Growth

paras: Businesses often consider transport access when choosing a location. More frequent services can shorten the time passengers wait.
New transit lines can affect demand for nearby housing and commercial property. Passengers value dependable services as well as fast journeys.
A common ticketing system can make transfers between operators easier. Building new infrastructure can temporarily disrupt current travel patterns.
Transit performs differently depending on how homes, jobs and services are arranged. Some economic and social effects emerge only after several years.
